jobs.title: Strategic Finance Manager
jobs.description:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

Position Summary

Antora Energy is seeking a highly analytical and driven Strategic Finance to own and operate the company’s core financial model, deliver mission-critical insights that guide strategic decisions, and support capital markets engagement. This role sits at the center of Antora’s commercial, operational, and product teams—translating fast-moving inputs into clear, data-driven outputs for executives, investors, and partners.

The ideal candidate thrives in complexity, is comfortable operating independently, loves solving new problems, and brings the rigor of an investment banking background to the challenge of scaling a climate-tech company. This is a high-visibility role with significant opportunities for growth, learning, and impact.

Roles & Responsibilities

Strategic Finance

- Own Antora’s corporate financial model (working cross functionally to collect real-time inputs, creating model scenarios, and producing insights for Antora leadership)

- Translate updated inputs into clear, actionable outputs that inform executive decision-making.

- Guide strategic planning by collaborating with colleagues across Antora, including Operations (production forecasting), Engineering (product inputs), and Commercial (growth targets)

- Deliver rapid scenario analysis and insights to guide strategic decision processes.

Capital Markets

-

- Support capital raising processes from end to end.

- Develop and refine investor materials, translating complex technical and financial concepts into crisp, clear narratives

- Guide due diligence workflows, collecting inputs from internal colleagues and delivering answers to prospective investors

- Manage investor engagement, data rooms, and transaction closing processes

Key Qualifications

- 4+ years of professional experience, ideally with some experience in an investment banking environment.

- Demonstrated mastery of complex financial modeling, scenario analysis, and quantitative problem-solving.

- Ability to synthesize cross-functional inputs and communicate insights quickly and clearly.

- High attention to detail with the ability to operate in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

- Excellent written communication and presentation skills.

Additional Qualifications Desired

- Prior experience in power & utilities, infrastructure, industrials, or energy sectors.

- Familiarity with hardware-enabled or manufacturing-intensive business models.

- Location: Strong preference for San Francisco Bay Area (San Jose or SF) for closer collaboration and coaching.

Work Location:  Onsite - San Jose, CA

Salary Range:  $148,000 USD - $173,000 USD

Sala ry Basis:  Annual

Please note that the salary range listed above reflects Antora Energy's estimated pay for this position. The actual salary offered will be within the posted range and determined based on several factors including but not limited to a candidate's experiences, credentials and expertise, as they pertain to the position's requirements.

In addition to a competitive base salary, Antora Energy’s Total Rewards program includes equity compensation in the form of stock options, a premium health benefits package with life and disability insurance, a 401K plan with employer contributions, flexible spending accounts, and an industry leading paid-time-off policy that features flexible and inclusive holiday observance, as well as paid volunteer time off.

#LI-Onsite
When it comes to stopping climate change, we need everyone. We believe that having a diversity of backgrounds and experiences strengthens all of us, and we strive to create an environment where every one of us is empowered to create meaningful change.

jobs.title: Principal, Power Procurement
jobs.description:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

Position Summary

The Principal, Power Procurement will lead complex utility tariff negotiations, originate off-take agreements with utilities, and set consistently high standards for deal execution across the Energy team. This role combines deep, hands-on deal negotiations and ownership, with mentorship for a growing team of deal leads who negotiate energy service agreements, custom tariffs, infrastructure arrangements with utilities, and power purchase agreements across multiple ISOs. The Principal will set deal standards, architect first-of-kind commercial structures, and serve as a trusted escalation point for resolving negotiations aligned with business objectives.

Roles & Responsibilities

-
Deal Leadership & Origination

- Lead marquee negotiations for utility tariffs and energy service agreements across US markets, including novel tariff structures, custom rate arrangements, and non-standard commercial terms.

- Originate capacity and power sales, including negotiating MOUs, term sheets, and off-take agreements with hyperscalers, utilities, and other large-load customers.

- Architect first-of-kind deal structures tailored to Antora's unique load profile, flexible, dispatchable thermal energy storage, navigating ambiguity where precedent doesn't exist.

- Serve as the primary escalation point for deal team members when negotiations encounter novel risks, counterparty resistance, or deviations from established playbooks.

- Coordinate with Finance, Legal, Policy, and Engineering to align commercial terms with project economics, risk appetite, and technical constraints.

Team Mentorship & Deal Standards

- Mentor and develop deal leads across utility negotiations, providing coaching on negotiation strategy, counterparty management, contract redlining, and commercial judgment.

- Establish and maintain deal standards: term sheet templates, negotiation playbooks, deviation thresholds, and risk escalation frameworks that enable the team to execute efficiently while maintaining quality.

- Conduct regular deal reviews, providing substantive feedback on models, redlines, and negotiation positioning; raise the bar on the quality of decision memos and internal deal presentations.

- Build a culture of commercial rigor, ensuring the team can articulate the "why" behind every material term and defend Antora's positions with data and market context.

Utility & Counterparty Relationships

- Build and maintain senior-level relationships with utility executives, regulatory stakeholders, and key counterparties across priority ISOs/RTOs.

- Represent Antora in high-stakes utility meetings, regulatory workshops, and industry forums where commercial credibility and deep expertise matter.

- Partner with Business Development to qualify and advance opportunities, ensuring smooth handoffs from early engagement to active negotiation.

Strategic Input

- Advise the VP, Energy on market-level commercial strategy, including where to deploy negotiating resources, which tariff pathways to prioritize, and how deal terms should evolve as the business scales.

- Identify patterns across deals, common counterparty objections, emerging tariff structures, regulatory shifts, and translate these into proactive strategy adjustments and playbook updates.

- Support investor discussions and project financings by providing credible, experienced perspective on commercial deal structures and pipeline quality.

Key Qualifications

- 12+ years of experience in power procurement, energy origination, utility negotiations, or energy commercial roles, with a demonstrated track record of closing complex energy transactions.

- Closed 8+ PPAs, energy service agreements, or equivalent utility contracts; experience negotiating at least 3 original or custom tariff structures.

- Deep expertise in utility tariff design, wholesale power markets, and the commercial mechanics of how large loads contract for energy and grid services.

- Proven ability to mentor and elevate commercial teams, whether through formal management or as a senior IC who sets standards and coaches others.

- Experience negotiating with sophisticated counterparties (utilities, hyperscalers, IPPs) in multiple ISOs/RTOs; comfort navigating novel deal structures where precedent is limited.

- Strong commercial judgment with ability to balance speed, risk, and value capture in fast-moving deal environments.

- Exceptional communication skills, able to distill complex commercial dynamics into clear recommendations for leadership and external stakeholders.

Additional Qualifications Desired

- Experience with energy storage, thermal storage, or flexible load commercial structures.

- Background in storage, capacity sales, or hyperscaler energy procurement.

- Experience in high-growth or start-up environments where commercial processes and team structures are still being built.

- Existing senior relationships with utility procurement/rates teams and ISO/RTO stakeholders in MISO, SPP, ERCOT, or PJM.

Work Location:  Remote, US

Salary Range:  $217,000 USD - $260,000 USD

Sala ry Basis:  Annual

The actual salary offered will be within the posted range and determined based on several factors including but not limited to a candidate's experiences, credentials and expertise, as they pertain to the position's requirements.

jobs.title: Senior HR Generalist (Contract)
jobs.description:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

Position Summary

Antora is looking for an Senior HR Generalist / People Partner who combines hands-on ownership of day-to-day people operations with the judgment to manage more complex employee relations, manager coaching, and people-program work. This role is the primary point of contact for a defined group of employees and managers, running the operational engine of payroll, benefits, onboarding/offboarding, immigration, and leave administration, while also partnering with leaders on team effectiveness, organizational change, and moderately complex employee relations matters. It suits someone who is equally comfortable processing a payroll change in UKG and coaching a manager through a difficult conversation, and who can work independently while collaborating closely with the broader People Team.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees and managers, answering questions about HR programs, policies, and benefits, and escalating complex issues when needed.

- Manage employee onboarding and offboarding end-to-end (orientation to terminations) with a focus on employee experience.

- Own day-to-day HR operations: HRIS/UKG maintenance and reporting, payroll support, benefits administration, leave-of-absence (parental, FMLA, disability) and immigration case support) in partnership with outside counsel.

- Manage moderately complex employee relations matters — including workers' comp claims, investigations, and terminations — assessing risk and recommending solutions in partnership with legal and HR colleagues as needed.

- Partner with managers to support team effectiveness, performance, development, and engagement; provide coaching on people decisions and escalate complex issues to senior HR as needed.

- Support organizational design and change initiatives by identifying implications for people, advising on communications, and helping teams navigate transitions.

- Partner with leaders on workforce planning, headcount needs, and org health insights using people data and trends.

- Own or co-own the rollout of people programs (performance cycles, engagement initiatives, onboarding improvements, benefit enrollment, compensation planning, capability-building efforts).

- Interpret HR policies and employment law to guide decision-making across salaried and hourly populations, staying current on regulations, trends, and best practices.

- Strengthen cross-functional partnerships with HR Operations, Talent Acquisition, Payroll/Finance, and other teams to enable effective execution and continuous improvement.

- Lead or support other people-program projects and initiatives as needed.

Key Qualifications

- 5+ years of human resources or people operations experience supporting managers and employees in a fast-paced environment.

- Demonstrated ability to manage moderately complex employee relations and organizational challenges with increasing independence.

- Hands-on experience owning HR operational work (HRIS, payroll support, benefits, leave administration, immigration coordination) as well as advising managers on team-level decisions.

- Comprehensive knowledge of HR policies, best practices, and employment law across HR disciplines (performance, development, policy, org effectiveness).

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, both written and verbal.

- High discretion and judgment, with the ability to handle sensitive matters and employee data with impeccable attention to detail.

- Proven ability to build trust and collaborate across teams, and experience rolling out new people programs, processes, and policies.

Additional Qualifications Desired

- Experience providing HR support to employees in a manufacturing production environment.

- Experience in a fast-paced startup environment.

- PHR or SPHR certification.

- Experience with UKG.

Position Summary

The Business Development Analyst is an integral member of Antora’s international development team, providing essential support to senior team members focused on originating high-quality industrial decarbonization projects. These are large scale, often >$100M industrial energy projects requiring close technical and economic team collaboration across a broad internal and external team. This role involves identifying market opportunities, supporting customer onboarding and early project development, conducting initial financial modeling, and developing project proposals. Projects are mostly international, with initial focus in Spain and Australia, but will include projects in other countries including the US. The Analyst will also contribute to developing and streamlining processes and systems that enhance the development team’s efficiency and effectiveness.

- Support senior business development team members in identifying and assessing new market opportunities and project leads in targeted industrial sectors.

- Assist with onboarding industrial customers and managing early-stage project development activities to ensure successful project initiation.

- Conduct financial modeling and screening of potential projects to assess feasibility and profitability, including being able to structure project economics from energy bills, weigh the impacts of utility rate or capital costs changes, etc.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, project finance, and legal teams to gather insights and resources that drive successful project outcomes.

- Develop, format, and refine proposals and presentations to communicate project value propositions to customers and stakeholders.

- Support the creation and refinement of Business Development processes and systems, helping the team scale efficiently and maintain high productivity.

Key Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience in business development, finance, or a similar role, ideally within the industrial or energy sectors.

- Experience running energy project finance models from energy bill level data inputs

- Strong proficiency in modeling, market research, presentation building and data analysis.

- Strong quantitative and problem-solving abilities, with attention to detail.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience with proposal development.

- Ability to work collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment.

Additional Qualifications Desired

- Fluency in Spanish (nice to have but not required), ideally with working familiarity with technical energy language skill

- Familiarity with renewable energy markets, industrial decarbonization, or thermal applications.

- Experience with CRM software and project management tools.

Position Summary

Antora’s Project Finance team sits at the center of turning a rapidly expanding commercial pipeline into financed, executed projects. We're looking for a project finance professional to join a small, high-leverage team and own the economic analysis and underwriting behind this growing deal pipeline.

You'll bring 3+ years of project finance experience and the judgment to hit the ground running, underwriting complex energy and infrastructure deals, partnering with commercial development teams across verticals, and helping build the standardized tools and processes that let Antora underwrite consistently as we scale. Over time, you'll grow into leading project financing yourself.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Build, maintain, and stress-test project-level financial models across Antora’s commercial development verticals.

- Own economic analysis and underwriting for an active and growing pipeline, providing critical modeling bandwidth to the Project Finance team.

- Partner closely with commercial development, policy, strategy, and power-supply teams to standardize how projects are underwritten and ensure market learnings flow back into deal structuring.

- Develop templatized models and screening tools for the commercial teams, and train developers to use them effectively for early-stage evaluation.

- Support the investment-committee process, providing structured financial guidance as projects mature from early screening to signed term sheets and beyond.

- Contribute to the broader capital-raise effort as Antora builds repeatable financing facilities with preferred investors.

- Grow toward independently leading due diligence and negotiation on project financings over time.

Key Qualifications

- 3+ years of experience in project finance, energy/infrastructure finance, infrastructure investing, or a development-side finance role.

- Demonstrated mastery of project-level financial modeling; building models from scratch and using them to drive real decisions.

- Strong grasp of how commercial contracts, offtake agreements, and financing structures shape project economics.

- Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment full of innovative deals.

- Excellent cross-functional communication; able to advise and enable non-finance partners.

- A real passion for analytical and underwriting work; and the ability to teach it.

Additional Qualifications Desired
